function: SSDDQN (self-supervised double DQN) jointly selects the RIS phase-shift vector and the uplink transmit power of IoT devices to maximize energy efficiency under QoS constraints (pp. 1, 4).
system: Uplink: BS with 4 antennas, 3 single-antenna IoT devices, one passive reflecting RIS with 4-32 elements and quantized phases, 5 MHz, 3.5 GHz (pp. 3, 9, 10).
method: Self-supervised double DQN (replay buffer ordered by episodic reward), two hidden layers of 512 neurons; centralized reinforcement learning, 10,000 episodes (pp. 6, 8, 10).
data_channel: Simulated: SimRIS generator (outdoor) with path loss and Rician fading (kappa=10); random device positions per episode; 3GPP UMi cited only for time scales and 3.5 GHz (pp. 3-4, 9-10).
test_conditions: Testing uses other random channel seeds and device positions of the same simulator (p. 10); RIS size varied; training repeated at each carrier frequency (pp. 10, 12).
baselines: Non-learned: exhaustive search, branch and bound, SCA, and no-RIS; learned: traditional DDQN and PER-based DDQN (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Average energy efficiency (bit/Joule) versus RIS elements; execution time (s); convergence episodes; payload delivery (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Space complexity O(U x layers + D); execution time 0.69 s (DRL), 7.85 s (SCA), 89.36 s (BB); complexity versus device count in Table III (pp. 9, 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "is modeled as a Rician fading distribution, which can be" expressed; p. 9: "SimRIS Channel Simulator v2.0 in MATLAB, an open-source" tool. Not met: path loss plus Rician model; 3GPP UMi [45] is cited only for time scales and the 3.5 GHz carrier (p. 9), and the paper never says SimRIS follows TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 10: "factors to generate the channel states, and the positions of the" IoT devices change per episode, so test data are other random draws of the same simulator. Not met: no unseen scenario; p. 12: "We conducted the training phase using different 5G NR" carrier frequencies, i.e. training at each one.
q3_support: p. 10: "RIS-assisted IoT system between the proposed SSDDQN and" other algorithms; p. 11: "Table III compares the performance of various algorithms in" average EE: ES, BB, SCA (non-learned) and PER-based DDQN and DDQN (learned).
q4_support: p. 11: "achieve the lowest computational time of about 0.69 secs." (Fig. 6) and "the DRL-based algorithms increases linearly with the number" of IoT devices (Table III); p. 9: "O(U × ς + D). Here, D represents the size of the experience".
q5_support: p. 9: "SimRIS Channel Simulator v2.0 in MATLAB, an open-source" tool [41] generates the channels. Not met: no link to the authors' code or data, a public simulator is not a released dataset, and there is no measured data (pp. 1-16).
notes: Included, area 3: SSDDQN learns the RIS phase-shift vector and the IoT transmit powers (p. 1). q1 and q5 flagged for the reviewer: channels come from the open-source SimRIS simulator (p. 9), not described as built on TR 38.901, while Sec. II models path loss plus Rician fading (p. 4). q3 rests on EE comparisons with PER-based DDQN and DDQN (Fig. 5, Table III, p. 11).
